newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council calls for halt to Afghanistan fighting.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council calls for halt to Afghanistan fighting.

text.p: The Security Council expressed grave concern on Wednesday at the continued escalation of the conflict in Afghanistan and called for an immediate halt to the fighting.

A statement read at a brief council meeting also called on all Afghan parties to return to the negotiating table and to work for a broad-based, fully representative government that would protect the rights of all Afghans and abide by the country's international obligations.

The statement was a response to a recent report by Secretary-General Kofi Annan on the situation in Afghanistan where the fundamentalist Islamic Taliban movement, which captured Kabul, the capital, last September, controls more than two-thirds of the country and is battling an opposition alliance.

Annan said the warring parties seemed bent on resolving their problems through military means and had paid no at attention to the many calls for a ceasefire and dialogue made by the Security Council, the head of the U.N. mission in Afghanistan, Norbert Holl of Germany, and by others.
Annan said the conflict was increasingly being fuelled by strong ethnic feelings between the predominantly Pushtun Taliban and the Tajiks, Hazaras and Uzbeks who comprise the opposition camp.
The council statement said peace and stability could best be achieved through intra-Afghan political negotiations under U.N. auspices with the coordinated assistance of all countries concerned.
It stressed that all external interference must cease and called on all states to end immediately the supply of arms and ammunition to all parties.

The council said the continuation of the conflict provided a fertile ground for terrorism and illegal drug production and trafficking that destabilised the region and beyond, and called on Afghan leaders to halt such activities.
